avoid_when: Avoid for content-heavy slides or pages requiring charts, images, or detailed explanations.
Avoid when presenter, affiliation, and date metadata are unnecessary.
families.description: A formal branded cover centers a large title in a blue horizontal band above presenter and date metadata.
families.digest: branded cover with title band and metadata
families.name: cover-hero
selection_hints: Use as an opening slide for a formal academic, technical, or institutional presentation.
Choose when a single prominent title should be followed by centered presenter and date details.

avoid_when: Avoid when a detailed recap, contact information, or next steps are required.
Avoid for regular content slides with multiple information blocks.
families.description: A sparse branded closing page centered on one prominent thank-you statement across a blue horizontal band.
families.digest: closing thank-you message on blue band
families.name: closing-hero
selection_hints: Use as the final slide of a formal presentation.
Choose when a simple branded thank-you closing is sufficient.

avoid_when: Avoid when the chart must remain fully editable as native PowerPoint data.
Avoid for narratives without a quantitative comparison or supporting visual.
families.description: A titled evidence slide pairs concise analytical bullets on the left with a dominant comparison chart on the right.
families.digest: split analysis with large comparison chart
families.name: content-split
selection_hints: Use for a quantitative result supported by a large chart and concise interpretation.
Choose when readers need both visual evidence and a short written takeaway.
Works well for comparing several models, products, cohorts, or scenarios.

avoid_when: Avoid when the topic has no process, system, or workflow to visualize.
Avoid when the main visual must remain editable as separate diagram elements.
Avoid for image-led storytelling or minimal statement slides.
families.description: A titled split-layout content slide pairs a compact process summary with a large, detailed workflow diagram.
families.digest: workflow overview with bullets and process diagram
families.name: content-split
selection_hints: Use for explaining a workflow with a concise textual summary beside a detailed process visual.
Choose when readers need both high-level takeaways and a comprehensive system diagram.
Works well for technical, operational, or research process explanations.

avoid_when: Avoid when the visual must remain editable as native diagram elements.
Avoid when content requires multiple independent charts or dense data tables.
families.description: A top-titled content slide pairs explanatory bullets on the left with a large comparison diagram on the right.
families.digest: split explanation with supporting comparison diagram
families.name: content-split
selection_hints: Use for explaining a concept with concise points and one supporting visual.
Choose when a large diagram or illustrative comparison complements a short narrative.

avoid_when: Avoid when the visual is not the primary evidence.
Avoid for multiple charts or dashboard-style analysis.
families.description: A large central heatmap provides the evidence, followed by concise explanatory bullets beneath a prominent title.
families.name: content-title_body
selection_hints: Use for presenting one dominant analytical chart with concise interpretation.
Choose when a heatmap or matrix visualization needs supporting takeaways.

avoid_when: Avoid when the agenda needs descriptions, timings, owners, or multiple columns.
Avoid for a highly visual or image-led navigation page.
families.description: A formal agenda page presents the deck structure as a large, spacious bullet list beneath a compact heading.
families.digest: simple agenda with large bullet list
families.name: agenda-title_body
selection_hints: Use for a concise agenda with roughly four to six major sections.
Choose when a formal, spacious, single-column table of contents is appropriate.

avoid_when: Avoid when the content needs visuals, data charts, or side-by-side comparison.
Avoid when more than two main topic groups must be presented.
Avoid when the content needs charts, images, tables, or multiple independent panels.
Avoid when more than a few short hierarchical bullet groups are required.
families.description: A conventional content slide presents a prominent top heading above a spacious two-level bullet outline.
families.name: content-title_body
selection_hints: Use for a straightforward explanation organized into a few hierarchical bullet groups.
Choose when a topic can be summarized with short headings and supporting statements.
Use for a straightforward explanatory slide organized as a short hierarchical outline.
Use when two or three main ideas each need concise supporting points.
